ordered_diagnoses: Bile duct stricture due to metastatic disease

facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old woman
cervical cancer metastatic to paraaortic and left supraclavicular lymph nodes
paclitaxel and bevacizumab administered for 63 and 36 days before presentation, respectively
each followed the next day by cisplatin
marked elevation of liver enzymes: AST 173 U/L, ALT 221 U/L, γ-GTP 2553 U/L, and ALP 5188 U/L
Abdominal ultrasonography showed wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts and of the gallbladder, with bile-duct strictures and dilatations
Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed wall thickening of both extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts with luminal narrowing and dilation, and gallbladder wall thickening
Biopsy of the common bile duct showed no malignant cells and only modest infiltration of neutrophils
bile cytology was also negative for malignancy
Ursodeoxycholic acid was started on day 6
cholangiography via the drainage tube revealed strictures and dilatations with irregular wall contours in the intrahepatic bile ducts of both lobes
extrahepatic bile-duct changes were modest
